---
title: "What is the probability of event A given event B?"
---

## Question

What is the probability of event A given event B?

## Work through it

Define A and B; restrict to complete cases; count the rows meeting B, then the rows meeting both A and B; divide joint count by the B count.

## Worked example: airquality

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("airquality")
A <- d$Ozone > 60
B <- d$Temp >= 80
result <- ru_apply("conditional_probability", data=d, x=A, y=B,
                   event=TRUE, given=TRUE)
stopifnot(result["probability"]>=0,result["probability"]<=1)
```

The denominator consists only of complete observations with temperature at least 80°F; the numerator is the subset also exceeding the ozone threshold. Missing ozone measurements are excluded from both counts.

## Adapt to another question

```r
ru_apply("conditional_probability", data=your_data, x=your_data$A, y=your_data$B, event=TRUE, given=TRUE)
```

Reverse the condition only if the question asks P(B given A). The two conditional probabilities usually differ.

Check the input conditions with `ru_plan("conditional_probability")` before treating a calculation as an inference.
